research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; complaints, resident escalation, golden-thread information and key-building-information methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: PAP complaints-system duty
verified_claims: The principal accountable person must establish and operate a complaints system that allows residents and other building users to raise relevant complaints.
limitations: A complaints system's existence does not prove that individual complaints are handled effectively.

sources.name: Relevant-complaint scope
verified_claims: Relevant complaints concern structural failure, spread of fire or the performance of an accountable person.
limitations: A routine service or maintenance request must not automatically be classified as a relevant complaint.

sources.name: Seven-year complaint record
verified_claims: The PAP must keep a record of each relevant complaint for seven years.
limitations: A retention period does not establish that records are complete or accurate.

sources.name: Complaint record contents
verified_claims: The record must include complaint information, AP response steps, regulator involvement and the outcome.
limitations: Recorded fields do not prove the adequacy of the investigation or outcome.

sources.name: Recurring relevant complaint
verified_claims: More than one relevant complaint about the same issue within seven years is treated as a recurring relevant complaint.
limitations: Similarity between complaints requires issue-level evidence and must not be inferred from keywords alone.

sources.name: Fair and impartial treatment
verified_claims: The complaints system should support impartial and fair treatment of issues raised.
limitations: A policy statement is not proof that treatment was impartial in a particular case.

sources.name: Resident consultation on process
verified_claims: Residents should be involved and consulted when the complaints process is established or changed.
limitations: Consultation does not transfer statutory responsibility to residents.

sources.name: Complaints information duties
verified_claims: Residents must be told what a relevant complaint is, how to raise it, how it will be handled and expected investigation and response timings.
limitations: Published information does not prove that every resident received or understood it.

sources.name: BSR escalation route
verified_claims: The process must describe how and when issues can be escalated to BSR and provide contact details.
limitations: An escalation route does not mean BSR will accept every issue as a relevant complaint.

sources.name: Challenge and representative rights
verified_claims: People raising issues must be able to challenge responses and may appoint a representative when necessary.
limitations: Representation does not alter the evidential requirements for the complaint.

sources.name: Existing-system adaptation
verified_claims: An existing complaints system may be adapted; a separate building-safety complaints process is not always required.
limitations: Adaptation must still cover the statutory building-safety complaint requirements.

sources.name: Complaints policy publication
verified_claims: The PAP must publish a complaints policy explaining relevant complaints, responsibilities and how the system works.
limitations: Publication alone does not prove operational compliance.

sources.name: Latest policy distribution
verified_claims: The latest policy must be provided to accountable persons and residents, and other APs must understand and use the process.
limitations: A distribution claim requires delivery evidence and must not be inferred from file creation.

sources.name: Accessible complaint channels
verified_claims: Complaint information should be clearly displayed and accessible, with channels such as email, telephone, online and in person considered.
limitations: Availability of channels does not prove accessibility for every resident.

sources.name: Risk-prioritised handling
verified_claims: Complaints should be prioritised by identified risk rather than receipt order, tracked through investigation and answered with reasons, actions and timeframes.
limitations: Risk prioritisation requires case-specific assessment and must not be reduced to a generic queue score.
